title: Injective resolution agrees with its acyclic comparison
statement: Let C and D be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], with injective resolutions in C [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. If F:C→D is additive and preserves finite limits, then the canonical acyclic-resolution comparison for an injective resolution I of X equals I.isoRightDerivedObj F in every nonnegative degree.

source.place: Tags 015E and 06XR; InjectiveResolution.isoRightDerivedObj_hom_naturality and the defining acyclic-resolution comparison.

proof.text: Lift the identity from I to the chosen resolution R. Naturality of I.isoRightDerivedObj identifies the homology map of this lift with the usual resolution comparison. Both complexes have right-acyclic terms, so mapping the lift by F preserves its quasi-isomorphism.
The acyclic constructor is the target comparison composed with the inverse of that homology map. Substitute the naturality identity and cancel the homology isomorphism.

lean.statement:
theorem acyclic_comparison_of_injective
    {C : Type u} {D : Type u'} [Category.{v} C] [Category.{v'} D]
    [Abelian C] [HasInjectiveResolutions C] [Abelian D]
    (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits F]
    {X : C} (I : InjectiveResolution X) (p : ℕ) :
    F.rightDerivedObjIsoOfResolution I.ι
      (fun n ↦ Functor.rightAcyclic_of_injective (I.cocomplex.X n)) p =
    I.isoRightDerivedObj F p
